name: THOMAS CHACRA
tagline: Environmental bioengineer | Sustainability data, supplier ESG & carbon accounting
addressee: To the Hiring Team, ABB Electrification Distribution Solutions.
subject: Application: Global Procurement Sustainability Specialist (JR00050454), Electrification Distribution Solutions
paragraphs: A procurement organisation that can put a defensible number on a supplier's carbon performance, and then write it into a contract, is one that can actually change what its supply base does. Most of my work has been about producing exactly that: product carbon footprints, supplier ESG datasets, and the dashboards that hold up when somebody asks where the figure came from. ABB's Distribution Solutions procurement is running this at a scale where method matters, which is why I am applying.

In my previous experiences I have worked on both sides of the data. I built a cradle to grave product carbon model to ISO 14067, structuring supplier environmental data so that the improvement levers became visible rather than theoretical. As a sustainability analyst I worked on supplier sustainability assessment datasets and ESG benchmarking for client disclosure programmes, built KPI frameworks and Power BI dashboards, and automated a certification workflow that cut analysis time by around 70 percent. I have also worked to ISO 14001 and 45001 requirements and prepared a CSRD double materiality matrix, so the reporting and compliance side of this post is familiar ground.

What draws me to the role is the position it occupies. Scope 3 Category 1, EcoVadis coverage, SSBM and material compliance are not separate projects in a procurement organisation; they are the same conversation with category managers, held in the language of sourcing strategies and contracts. That is the part of sustainability work I find most durable, the point where a methodology becomes a clause and a clause becomes a supplier's next investment decision. Training buyers to read their own data is how that holds after the project ends.

I work fluently in English and French, with Dutch in progress, and I am at ease in MS365, particularly Excel and Power BI, alongside SQL and Python for the heavier data work. I am based in Brussels and would be glad to discuss how the location ABB confirms for this post could work in practice.

I would welcome the chance to discuss how the sustainability roadmap for ELDS procurement could be built on data your category teams already trust. Thank you for considering my application, and I am glad to provide any further detail you need.
